# Summary — NAV 0104 Approach Plates

**Source:** [NAV0104 Approach Plates](https://youtu.be/ddxMAtQdaa4) — Project ThreeSixty  
**YouTube title:** NAV0104   Approach Plates  
**Caption type:** Auto-generated (YouTube ASR); ASR errors preserved in `transcript.md`.

## Short summary
How to read **high and low** approach plates / playbooks (NGA / FAA sources also feeding ForeFlight & SkyVector): plate segments (header, plan view, profile, minima), MSA vs emergency safe altitude, ALS symbology, inoperative-components corrections, airport sketch / full-page diagram / hot spots, LAHSO notes for T-45, low-plate differences (OROCA when ESA absent), pilot-controlled lighting, glide-slope altitude checks at the FAF/OM, VDA / descent-gradient tables, and **PAR / ASR radar minima** including **+100 ft HAT bump for single-pilot / CNAF 3710**.

## Key takeaways
1. **Plate sources:** FAA.gov PDFs (high/low approaches + IFR charts); printed **NGA High Approach Playbook**; third-party apps pull from the same ultimate sources.
2. **Header block:** Approach title, airport ID, navaid/course data, runway length, TDZE / field elevation, **Trouble T** (takeoff issues), ALS code (e.g. **A5** with **dot** = sequenced flashers/strobes), narrative missed approach, frequencies in use order (ATIS → Approach → Tower → Ground → Clearance; radar type ASR/PAR if depicted).
3. **Plan view:** Often a **20 NM** to-scale circle; obstructions (MSL heights), holding entry at IAF, **MSA** (typically **25 NM** about the defining navaid; quadrant values) and **Emergency Safe Altitude** (**100 NM**; 1000 ft obstacle clearance flat / **2000 ft** in designated mountainous terrain).
4. **Profile:** Glidepath angle, **TCH** (AGL), glide-slope intercept altitude, pictorial missed approach matching the narrative, straight-in / circling minima lines.
5. **CNAF 3710 single-pilot weather:** Example Atlantic City high ILS — plate may show **18 RVR**, but **3710** needs **no lower than 24 RVR (~½ mi)**; military minima often shown in parentheses (e.g. **200-½**).
6. **Inoperative components:** Approach designed assuming all components (incl. lighting) work. Example: MALSR OTS → increase RVR to **4000 (~¾ mi)** per table / plate note — always check plate-specific notes.
7. **Airport sketch / full-page diagram:** Arresting gear, barriers, displaced threshold (usable for takeoff/rollout **not** touchdown), hotspot callouts, lat/long grid for building waypoints, runway gradient.
8. **Hot spots / LAHSO:** Explained in front matter of approach playbooks; example Atlantic City HS1. **T-45s are not really authorized for land-and-hold-short operations.**
9. **Low plates:** Same features generally; may omit ESA — use chart **OROCA** (same 1000/2000 ft clearance idea). **Pilot-controlled lighting** = black circle / white lettering ALS symbology.
10. **Glide-slope check:** At OM/FAF, centered GS should match published GS altitude (e.g. Tuscaloosa **1433**). Mismatch → suspect transmitter / altimeter / temp error; consider transitioning to **localizer** (start clock at FAF; use timing table).
11. **Descent gradient table** (inside back cover): e.g. ~**637 fpm** for **3°** path at **120 kt** GS.
12. **Radar minima (PAR):** Lookup alphabetically. Example Meridian PAR — add **+100 ft** to HAT/DA for single-pilot 3710 (e.g. published 100 ft HAT → plan **200 ft HAT** / higher DA). PAR without GS ≈ ASR technique with somewhat lower mins than straight ASR.
